summary.title: Severity Levels - PagerDuty Incident Response Documentation
summary.one_liner: You learn how PagerDuty classifies incidents into SEV-1 to SEV-5 levels, which ones count as major incidents, and how each level gets a typical response.
takeaways: Incidents are classified as SEV-1 through SEV-5, where lower numbers are more urgent.
Anything above SEV-3 (SEV-1 and SEV-2) is a major incident and gets the full incident response process; a lower-severity issue can still be escalated if it needs coordinated response.
When unsure between two severities, treat the incident as the higher one and debate the level later in the postmortem.
Each level has a typical response, from paging an Incident Commander for SEV-1/2 to a JIRA ticket for cosmetic SEV-5 bugs.
For your own docs, make severity definitions specific and metric-driven, often tied to the percentage of users or accounts affected.
summary.summary: This PagerDuty documentation page explains how to classify operational incidents using SEV levels, where lower numbers are more urgent and higher severities permit riskier fixes. It defines SEV-1 through SEV-5 in a table with example conditions and the typical response for each, such as paging an Incident Commander for major incidents or opening a JIRA ticket for cosmetic bugs. It also gives guidance to assume the higher severity when uncertain and to review the call in a postmortem. The closing note advises teams to write more specific, metric-based definitions for their own use.
